chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“Ihram begins from five appointed locations that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله established. It is not proper for a pilgrim performing hajj or ʿumrah to enter ihram before them or after them.

He appointed Dhā al-Ḥulayfah for the people of al-Madīnah, and it is Masjid al-Shajarah. He used to pray there and enter into the obligation of hajj; then when he left the mosque, proceeded, and al-Baydāʾ became level with him near the first milestone, he entered ihram.

And he appointed al-Juḥfah for the people of al-Shām, al-ʿAqīq for the people of Najd, Qarn al-Manāzil for the people of al-Ṭāʾif, and Yalamlam for the people of al-Yaman. No one should turn away from the appointed places set by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.”

key_terms.ذَا ٱلْحُلَيْفَةِ: the miqāt appointed for the people of al-Madīnah
key_terms.قَرْنَ ٱلْمَنَازِلِ: the miqāt appointed for the people of al-Ṭāʾif
key_terms.مَوَاقِيتَ: appointed boundary points or designated places for entering ihram
key_terms.يَلَمْلَمَ: the miqāt appointed for the people of al-Yaman
key_terms.ٱلْإِحْرَامُ: the state of ritual consecration entered for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.ٱلْجُحْفَةَ: the miqāt appointed for the people of al-Shām
key_terms.ٱلْعَقِيقَ: the miqāt appointed for the people of Najd

ai.seo_question: What are the appointed miqats for entering ihram in hajj and ʿumrah?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the five designated mawāqīt from which a pilgrim must enter ihram for hajj or ʿumrah. It emphasizes adherence to the appointed locations established by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and identifies the specific miqāt for different regions.
